title: Guided Adventure and Exploration in Chattanooga
description: Guide to guided tours and in Chattanooga including ghost tours, food tours, kayaking, and historical experiences.
body: ; Download PDF Guide On your last trip you're at your third tourist trap, lines couldn't be any longer, you're sure your tickets are in your back left pocket (where they always are darnnit!) but now your scrambling to filter your gmail for them. Your spouse is agitated, and if they're agitated then by all means you have ground to be piping hot! Apologies for the projection. If you've been there before, let's you and I not let that happen again. But we don't pass that torch to just anyone, we're handing it off to a professional Chattanoogan. Someone who made it their mission to deliver a top-shelf customer experience on a topic they naturally feel passion towards. Should you want to: Explore the famed Chattanooga outdoors without worrying if you're still on the right trail an hour in. Dine at local favorite restaurants without trying to figure out the best times and tables. Learn the cities history and take the sights of well known landmarks with the efficiency and enthusiasm of professional guide. See a bat cave via kayak, or ghosts via walking Then there's a guided adventure out there for you. If none of those grabbed you we've included a few other options for your consideration. By Topic . City & History Outdoor Adventures Food & Entertainment City & History . Chattanooga Trolley Tours . Take a journey on city tour in a nostalgic vintage tour bus. The captivating red and green colored trolley and wood lined interior provide an inviting environment to take in the city sights and sounds while you listen to your local guides descriptions of the city of Chattanooga. Trolley tours can be anywhere from 75 minutes to up to 4 hours in length depending on the tour option you elect. You'll come away with intimate details on the stories, history, and maybe a few tall tales that have come to make Chattanooga what it is today. For those visiting in the summer months rest assured the vehicle has A/C and is enclosed. The Trolley is not short on tour options: 1. Derailed Adventure (&126;$49). This is the big ticket item, a trolley tour paired with a ride through history on a historic train. 2. Legends & Shadows (&126;$32). Take the trolley on a different kind of Chattanooga tour, one for the true crime and haunted history enthusiasts. 3. Express Trolley (&126;$29). A condensed one-hour city overview for those in a time crunch, hitting downtown, the riverfront, and the Chattanooga Choo Choo. 4. Coker Museum & Trolley Tour (&126;$42). Enjoy the classic trolley ride with an added visit to the Coker Automotive Museum for vintage cars and bikes. Nobody refers to these as 'the tour four' but they could be. If you're interested in getting to know the city and it's history in detail hopefully one of those piqued your interest. Check their website for booking information as the tour schedules can vary. You can also do your own private tour with advanced planning. Boasting a 4.9 Google Review, this guided adventure is a fan favorite for people of all ages. Chattanooga Trolley Tours vintage bus, perfect for exploring the city's history and landmarks. Chattanooga Ghost Tours . Chattanooga was grounds for prominent civil war battles, with cemeteries of the time still operating. The Trail of Tears, which the city played a large role in, added another tragedy passage to its complex history. Hauntings and paranormal are still rumored to this day from murders and events that occurred generations ago. Those facts can only mean one thing, epic ghost tours. Okay maybe there's more than one conclusion to draw but you get the point. With this storied history comes some fun ghost tours etched in fact and folklore and one of the more popular businesses running these adventures is Chattanooga Ghost Tours. Not only can you do a walking ghost tour, but they also offer ghost hunting options for some added excitement for the brave. At the time of last update they have a Murder and Mayhem Haunted History walking tour, UTC + Cemetery Ghost Hunt, and a Walking + Hunt Combo tour for those who want the best of both worlds. 1. Murder and Mayhem Haunted History walking tour. Take two hours in your evening to explore downtown Chattanooga through haunted history and tall tales of Chattanoga's past. 2. UTC Cemetery Ghost Hunt (hunting equipment included). Are you really going to pass up an opportunity to ghost hunt? I hope you have a good reason. Otherwise take a 1.5 hour hunting tour around the UTC campus with a stop at the Citizens Cemetery (if ghost hunting was scary enough on its own). 3. Walking Ghost Tour/Hunt Combo. A 1.5 hour combined tour for the best of both worlds if you couldn't choose just one. Additional note : They also run extended small-group Deluxe tours that include refreshment stops inside haunted locations. Check their calendar for current dates. The tours are designed for all ages. The walking ghost tours are rain or shine so be prepared with an appropriate jacket for any inclement weather conditions. Tour available can be found on the Chattanooga Ghost Tours website. Chattanooga Ducks . Here's a tour that can't decide if it's a bus or a boat, so it's both. Chattanooga Ducks loads you into a restored WWII amphibious "Duck," rolls through downtown for a narrated city tour, then drives straight down a ramp and splashes into the Tennessee River. Once you're afloat you'll get views of downtown, the riverfront, and the Maclellan Island wildlife sanctuary. It runs about an hour, works for all ages, and the corny-in-a-good-way narration is half the fun. Tours leave from 151 Riverfront Parkway and start around $36 per person. Check their website for the current schedule and to reserve a seat. Chattanooga Rydables Tours . If a trolley feels too tame and a walking tour too slow, split the difference on a Rydable. These are plush motorized scooters, and yes, some of them look like unicorns and dragons, so leave your dignity at the hotel and just have fun with it. A guide leads your group across the Walnut Street Bridge and through downtown, feeding you history and trivia along the way. The one-hour "Bridge to Fun" ride starts around $55, and the 1.5-hour "From Trains to Bridges" tour (which swings by the Chattanooga Choo Choo) runs about $75. They're open seven days a week and tours sell out, so book ahead. Browse routes and reserve on the Chattanooga Rydables website. Outdoor Adventures . Bat Cave Sunset Kayak Tour . Searching for outdoor activities in Chattanooga? How about Kayaking? How about Kayaking to watch up to 100,000 gray bats exit their cave for a nightly insect hunt? If don't have a deep rooted bat phobia (chiroptophobia), and you are a seeker of outdoor novelty this could be your chance to create some lasting memories. If you're in Chattanooga between March - October you can book this one of a kind tour. Their online reviews go on about what a fun experience this is, currently boasting a 5.0 star rating. Keep your eyes open for other wildlife you might get lucky to see on the paddle such as bald eagles, deer, river otter, and osprey. No previous kayaking experience for you or a group member? The 3 mile route is considered easy, and your guides will provide instructions. Anyone having difficulty can ask to be towed. Still worried about your lack of Kayaking experience? Maybe this review from Mimi Maxwell can offer some relief "... Katie was our guide and she was wonderful. Our group had 2 who had never been in a kayak before and she was very patient and helpful." Bring up to 20 people on your tour to share the adventure with your loved ones (or loved ones in the making, for the newly dating). Some additional details: Tour season: Ongoing from March to early October Tour time: Tours run about 2 hours and start around 7:30pm Meeting Location: Maple View Recreation Area, Mapleview Rd, South Pittsburg, TN 37380 What to bring: Rain jacket weather dependent, a pre-filled up water bottle Individual ticket price: ~$77 (but subject to change) Learn more about these tours and book yours on the Chattanooga Guided Adventures website. Bonus Idea: If you end up loving the bat cav tour, or you don't happen to be in town in the right months, this same company runs a Sandhill Crane viewing tour from November through Februrary where you can view thousands of seasonal cranes on Hiwassee Island on the Tennessee River. Learn about the once endangered species comeback and why they make a stop in our area on their migration. For more self-guided outdoor adventures, check out our Chattanooga Outdoors Guide with 71 hiking, biking, and paddling routes. Chickamauga Battlefield Tour Options . Learn about this pivotal battle in the Civil War, which might still be an understatement. The battle of Chickamauga was a turning point in the war and the second most deadly battle next to Gettysburg. They have both guided and self guided tour options for you to explore and learn in this US National Park. Tour times are subject to change depending on guide availability, but typically group tours run on Saturdays and Sundays at 10AM and 2PM and tend to last about 90 minutes. The National Park Service has put together a guided tour that includes eight different points of interest. Drive or walk it, the grounds are beautiful, well maintained, and home to a lot of wildlife. To access the tour download the National Park Service app on your mobile device search for the Chickamauga Battlefield. Frankly, it's not the most user friendly app in the store. If you have trouble, the people at the visitors center can be very helpful, and they'll also provide you with a park map. Private Tour Option: Robert Carter, an author and historian offers private tours of the park, learn more on his website . Hiking Tours by Experience Chattanooga . Not sure if you've heard the news but Chattanooga has a great outdoor scene. If you're not exactly sure which trails and parks you want to explore on your visit (or days off work for our local readers), we suggest looking into guided hikes provided by Experience Chattanooga. Nearing 200 5 star reviews, chances are it will be time well spent. They variety of options for exploration, but a few cherry picked ones include: Good Morning Mountains. For waking up early and starting your day with panoramic views of the city and Tennessee River Gorge. There's also a different offering that includes an Alpaca farm. Soul Therapy. For a hike and tour of one of Tennessee's top waterfall trails. The Best of Tennessee. Their premium, longer outing for folks who want to see the region's greatest hits in a single guided day. Idea for Families: Their Alpacas, Mountains and Coffee option offers an opportunity to feed alpaca's and grab a coffee after your morning hike at Rosie Mae’s Alpaca Farm. You'll be picked up in the morning and all is concluded by lunchtime. They have more offerings on their website , check it out to book your tour and get more information. All tours are private and run by two lifelong Chattanoogans. A bonus included in your tour booking is professional photography throughout the trip, and you might like to know they donate a portion of their proceeds to the parks and communities in the area. Raccoon Mountain Caverns . Chattanooga's most famous cave is Ruby Falls, but about eight miles west of downtown there's a quieter one worth your time. Raccoon Mountain Caverns runs guided tours through a living cave full of stalactites, flowstone, and formations you won't find on the paved tourist routes. The Crystal Palace Walking Tour is the easy option, about 45 to 55 minutes along lit paths with steps and handrails, running roughly $29 for adults and $19 for kids. If you'd rather crawl than stroll, their Wild Cave tours hand you a helmet and light and send you deeper into the mountain, with two-hour, three-hour, and four-hour expeditions priced around $35, $45, and $55. It's open daily, and the wild tours are a genuinely different way to spend an afternoon. See tour times and book on the Raccoon Mountain Caverns website. Food & Entertainment . Trolley Pub Chattanooga . Fresh air, city and mountain views, your favorite beverage or two, and some light exercise make for a heck of an afternoon on the Trolley Pub. Bring your own elixir of choice and get out to explore the city in unique fashion. While out getting your thirst fixers, make sure you download music in advance, the company operates on the Bring Your Own Playlist model. You can connect to their bluetooth speakers and play your groups favorite songs. Your tour guide will point out interesting historic and modern day relevant landmarks as you drink, pedal, listen, and sightsee. If you're worried about pedaling for two hours straight, we can offer some peace of mind. Along the way you'll take a multiple breaks stopping at some of Chattanooga's best bars and restaurants. The pub is a popular group activity can fit up to fourteen people if you opt for a private tour, check out their website for scheduling. Group tour pricing ranges between $300-375 at the time of our last update. Another option is to get individual tickets for their Mixer Tour, where you and a group of like minded party bikers will explore the city my pedaling together. At the time of last update these tickets cost in the range of ~$25-30. Trolley Pub events are rain or shine so be sure to check the forecast and bring appropriate clothing. The Mixer Tours are for adults 21+ and for private tours the minimum age for passengers is 15. You may need to call a babysitter for a couple of hours for this one. Southern Belle . One of Chattanooga's most popular date-night options or a place to bring family for dinner when they're in town is the Southern Belle. Forget waterfront restaurant, take the water on the road with you as this historic paddle wheel riverboat leaves port traveling the Tennessee River for a scenic fun-filled evening. The southern charm of the vessel will transport you in time to the early 19th century. When these vessels weren't used for transportation, they were luxury cruises only available to the wealthy class. The Southern Belle is a modern sightseeing tribute that moment in time. The Southern Belle company offers many touring options that vary in length. One of the more popular is the Sunset Cruise, a 1.5 hour river ride where you can grab a glass of wine from the concession, kick back, and watch the light fade over the water. It starts around $36 per person. Some of their other cruising options include a narrated Sights Cruise, a romantic two-hour Sip & Sail with dinner and wine pairings, dinner cruises, and Maclellan Island eco tours, amongst many other options for your party. Check their website for more listings and availability. Food Tour . Finding the right places to eat in any city can be an overwhelming task, why not leave it to a professional through Chatt Taste. They provide private tours, events, and at the time of writing three distinct group tours for varied Chattanooga culinary experiences: Downtown Chattanooga Food Tour. Explore downtown Chattanooga's food scene and learn about our city exploratory adventure. Historic Southside Food Tour. Explore Historic Southside food offerings in this two hour guided adventure. ChattaBrunch Food Tour. Can you guess what this ones about? It's hard to go wrong with a mid morning combination of food, art, history and mimosas. More offerings and detailed information on the restaurants and individual tour details are available on their website linked below as they are subject to periodic change. This is another tour company with a 5 star review set. Previous foodies rave about their experiences with the various hosts and call out their knowledge and friendliness. If you're thinking about signing up for one, you can browse all their current tours here . Guided Tours Summary . 🚐 Tour 📍 Description 🚌 Chattanooga Trolley Tours Vintage bus tours covering Chattanooga history, folklore, or trains—great for families and history buffs. 👻 Chattanooga Ghost Tours Spooky walking tours, ghost hunts with equipment, and extended Deluxe tours with refreshment stops. 🦆 Chattanooga Ducks Narrated WWII amphibious duck boat that tours downtown then splashes into the Tennessee River. 🛴 Chattanooga Rydables Guided motorized-scooter tours across the Walnut Street Bridge and through downtown. 🚲 Trolley Pub Chattanooga Pedal-powered BYOB group tours with music and stops at local bars—great for adult outings. 🚢 Southern Belle Riverboat Dinner and scenic cruises on a historic riverboat with options like sunset, sights, and Sip & Sail. 🦇 Bat Cave Sunset Kayak Guided kayak trip to watch 100,000 bats emerge at sunset. Beginner-friendly and highly rated. 🪖 Chickamauga Battlefield Tours Ranger-led or self-guided tours via the NPS app or with local historians through preserved battlefields. 🥾 Experience Chattanooga Hikes Private hiking tours with photography and local guides. Includes alpaca visits, waterfalls, and panoramic overlooks. 🕯️ Raccoon Mountain Caverns Guided cave walks past living formations, plus wild spelunking crawls deeper into the mountain. 🍴 Chatt Taste Food Tours Curated food tours of downtown and the Southside. Also offers brunch tours with art and mimosas. Other Guides . Cloudland Canyon State Park Outdoor Adventures Sweet Treats

title: Market at Erlanger Medical Mall
description: The Chattanooga Market at Erlanger Medical Mall every Wednesday, 10:30am–1:30pm in Lobby A. Fresh produce, local art, and live music. Free admission.
body: The Chattanooga Market runs at Erlanger Medical Mall every Wednesday from 10:30am to 1:30pm. Find it in Lobby A. Fresh produce, local art, and live music in a hospital atrium. Free to browse, no ticket needed.

title: Chattanooga Market - River Market
description: The Chattanooga Market at Tennessee Aquarium Plaza every Saturday. Fresh produce, local art, live music, and food vendors on the downtown riverfront. Free admission.
body: The Chattanooga Market sets up at the Tennessee Aquarium Plaza every Saturday from 10am to 5pm. Fresh produce, local vendors, art, and live music on the downtown riverfront. Free admission. It draws a consistent Saturday crowd year round.

title: Amber Wallin
description: Comedian Amber Wallin performs a special engagement at The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Amber Wallin runs a special engagement at The Comedy Catch. Her set digs into adult themes with a blunt, honest edge. Plan a grown up night out downtown at 29 Station Street. The show starts at 7:00 PM, so arrive early and grab a drink.

title: Chris Higgins
description: Comedian Chris Higgins performs two nights of stand-up at The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Chris Higgins plays two nights at The Comedy Catch. You can grab the 7:00 PM or 9:15 PM show on either date. His comedy is rated R, so expect an adult crowd and blunt jokes. Book early since the late set fills up.

title: Claude Stuart
description: Comedian Claude Stuart performs two nights of stand-up at The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Two nights of adult stand up from Claude Stuart hit The Comedy Catch. Shows run at 7:00 PM and 9:15 PM on both dates. Plan a grown up night out downtown at 29 Station Street. Pick your time and get there early.

title: Graeson McGaha
description: Comedian Graeson McGaha performs a special engagement at The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga. This show is sold out.
body: Graeson McGaha headlines a special engagement at The Comedy Catch, and this one is sold out. Watch the venue page for any seats they release. The set leans adult, so leave the kids at home. Doors open before the 7:00 PM start.

title: Jenny Zigrino
description: Comedian Jenny Zigrino brings her rated-R stand-up to The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga for two nights.
body: Two nights and two shows each bring plenty of bite from Jenny Zigrino at The Comedy Catch. You can catch the 7:00 PM or 9:15 PM set on either date. Her comedy is rated R and runs bold. Book the time that fits your night.

title: Jonnie W
description: Clean comedy headliner Jonnie W performs at The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga. This show is sold out.
body: Clean, family friendly jokes are Jonnie W's calling card at The Comedy Catch. This show is sold out, so check the venue for released seats. Doors open before the 6:00 PM start. Show up early if you land a last minute ticket.

title: Josh Pray
description: Comedian Josh Pray performs a special engagement at The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Big bits and viral energy carry Josh Pray's set at The Comedy Catch. He works fast and leans physical, so the room stays loud. The show starts at 7:00 PM downtown at 29 Station Street. Come early and settle in for the ride.

title: Ontonio Kareem
description: Comedian Ontonio Kareem plays two nights of stand-up at The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Ontonio Kareem takes two nights at The Comedy Catch. Shows run at 7:00 PM and 9:15 PM on both dates. His set is rated R and moves quick. Pick the time that works, and bring a crowd that likes adult humor.

title: Southeaster City Slam
description: Southeaster City Slam is a weekly competitive comedy series at The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Local comics go head to head each week at Southeaster City Slam. They battle for laughs, and the crowd helps crown the winner. Expect rough edges, fresh jokes, and a fast pace. The show is rated R, so leave the kids at home.

title: Tanael Joachim
description: Stand-up comic Tanael Joachim brings his sharp storytelling to The Comedy Catch in Chattanooga.
body: Sharp storytelling and quick crowd work fill Tanael Joachim's set at The Comedy Catch. He pulls punchlines from real life and reads the room fast. The show starts at 7:00 PM downtown at 29 Station Street. Get there early for a good seat.

title: American Grappling Federation
description: The American Grappling Federation holds a jiu-jitsu and grappling tournament at the Chattanooga Convention Center on September 19, 2026.
body: The American Grappling Federation brings a jiu-jitsu and submission grappling tournament to the Convention Center on September 19. Competitors face off across gi and no-gi brackets. Come to watch the matches or sign up to compete. Check the AGF website for divisions, registration, and the day's schedule.

title: Animeverse
description: Animeverse anime convention comes to the Chattanooga Convention Center in August 2026.
body: Animeverse brings an anime convention to the Chattanooga Convention Center in August. Expect panels, cosplay, vendors, and a crowd that takes it seriously. Check the Animeverse website for exact dates, ticketing, and the full programming schedule.

title: Chattanooga Kidney Foundation - Dare to Dance
description: The Chattanooga Kidney Foundation hosts its Dare to Dance fundraiser at the Chattanooga Convention Center on October 3, 2026.
body: Dare to Dance is the Chattanooga Kidney Foundation's yearly fundraiser at the Convention Center on October 3. Local dancers take the floor to raise money for kidney patients and their families. Expect performances, an evening program, and a good cause behind it all. Check the Chattanooga Kidney Foundation website for tickets and table details.

title: Flip Trade Show
description: The Flip Trade Show comes to the Chattanooga Convention Center on August 15, 2026 — 100+ vendor tables of sports cards, Pokémon, TCGs, comics, Funko Pops, and collectibles.
body: Over 100 vendor tables of sports cards, Pokémon, Magic: The Gathering, comics, Funko Pops, video games, coins, and memorabilia spread across the Convention Center on August 15. Doors open at 11am. Bring a box if you're selling, bring a list if you're hunting. Check thefliptradeshow.com for vendor registration and admission details.

title: Steve Gonsalves Live: A Life with Ghosts
description: Ghost Hunters veteran Steve Gonsalves brings his live show A Life with Ghosts to the Chattanooga Convention Center on September 10.
body: Steve Gonsalves from Ghost Hunters brings his live show to the Chattanooga Convention Center on September 10. He shares stories from years of paranormal investigation — cases, evidence, and what it's actually like to do that work for a living. Check the convention center site for tickets.

title: The Pink Bride Show
description: The Pink Bride Show returns to the Chattanooga Convention Center on September 6, 2026, connecting engaged couples with local wedding vendors.
body: Photographers, caterers, florists, venues, and every other vendor you need for a wedding, all in one room at the Convention Center on September 6 from noon to 4pm. General admission is free. VIP bundle available at checkout if you want the extras. Find the vendor lineup at thepinkbride.com.

title: Meet the Microorganisms
description: Get under a microscope and discover what lives in the soil at Crabtree Farms in Chattanooga.
body: Get under a microscope and look at what's actually living in the soil. Crabtree Farms runs these hands-on science workshops for curious adults — no background required. $30 covers the session.

title: Meet the Microorganisms
description: Microscope workshop exploring soil biology at Crabtree Farms in Chattanooga.
body: Second run of the microscope workshop if August filled up. Same hands-on look at what lives in healthy soil — with the fall season giving the samples a different character than summer.

title: Monarch Magic: How to Support Butterflies in Your Backyard
description: Learn the Monarch butterfly migration and how to support them in your backyard at Crabtree Farms.
body: Learn the Monarch's migration story and what you can actually do in your yard to help. Crabtree's workshops lean practical — you'll leave with specific plants to grow and habitat tips you can act on.

title: Nature as Teacher: A Mindfulness Practice
description: Monthly mindfulness and meditation session rooted in nature at Crabtree Farms in Chattanooga.
body: A monthly gather at the farm for meditation rooted in the natural world. An hour outside, quiet, with a guide — easier to commit to than a studio class and more grounding than most.

title: Plant Identification and Foraging
description: Guided foraging and plant identification walk at Crabtree Farms in Chattanooga.
body: A guided walk through the farm property covering foraging fundamentals and plant ID. Good for beginners who want to learn what's edible and what isn't — with someone who actually knows the difference.

title: Sourdough Bagels
description: Hands-on sourdough bagel baking workshop at Crabtree Farms in Chattanooga.
body: Crabtree's baking workshops fill fast. This one covers sourdough bagel technique from scratch — mixing, shaping, boiling, baking. Beginners welcome, experienced bakers will still find it worth the trip.

title: KIDCON
description: KIDCON at the Creative Discovery Museum on September 18 is a superhero-themed family night for members from 6 to 8pm.
body: Suit up for KIDCON at the Creative Discovery Museum on September 18, from 6 to 8pm. The whole family can dress as their favorite superheroes for a night of games and hands-on fun across the museum. Members only, so bring your card and your cape.

title: Member Morning
description: Member Morning at the Creative Discovery Museum on August 23 opens the museum early for members from 9 to 10am. Free, but registration is required.
body: The Creative Discovery Museum opens early just for members on August 23, from 9 to 10am. Get a full hour with the exhibits before the doors open to everyone else. It costs nothing, but you must register first, so sign up ahead of time and bring your card.

title: Preschool Adventure: Superheroes!
description: Preschool Adventure: Superheroes! at the Creative Discovery Museum runs September 12 from 9 to 11am. A morning of superhero fun made for little kids.
body: The Creative Discovery Museum hosts a superhero morning for preschoolers on September 12, from 9 to 11am. Little kids can play, explore, and pretend to save the day. The event is free for members.

title: 3 Sisters Bluegrass Festival
description: The 3 Sisters Bluegrass Festival returns to Ross's Landing in Chattanooga on October 2-3, 2026. Free admission, local and national bluegrass acts on the Tennessee River.
body: Free bluegrass on the riverfront, two days, rain or shine. Chattanooga Presents books local, regional, and national acts every fall at Ross's Landing. Rhonda Vincent is confirmed for 2026. Lawn chairs and blankets welcome. No outside food, drink, or coolers. Vendors on site with food, beer, and wine. Leashed dogs OK. Free electric shuttle runs until 11pm. Downtown hotels are a short walk if you're making a weekend of it.

title: 4 Bridges Arts Festival
description: The 4 Bridges Arts Festival brings 140+ juried artists and $15,000+ in cash awards to First Horizon Pavilion in Chattanooga. One of the top 30 fine art festivals in the country.
body: 140+ juried artists fill First Horizon Pavilion on the Southside every spring. The 2026 edition awarded $15,000+ in cash prizes, judged by Elizabeth Ruffner, Lauren Nye of the Hunter Museum, and Raquel Mullins of Wavelength Space. The festival ranks in the top 30 fine art shows in the country. Saturday runs 10am–6pm, Sunday 10am–5pm. $6 at the gate, students and under 18 free. A ticketed Preview Party with wine and hors d'oeuvres runs Friday evening. The festival also includes an Emerging Artist program for local artists within 45 miles of Chattanooga.

title: Chattanooga Bacon & Barrel Festival
description: The Chattanooga Bacon & Barrel Festival brings 20+ local restaurants and 20+ distilleries to First Horizon Pavilion on September 26. Unlimited bacon dishes, whiskey samples, and a vote for the Golden Hog award. 21+ only.
body: Twenty-plus local restaurants compete for the Golden Hog award. Bulleit, Buffalo Trace, Crown Royal, and 17 more distilleries are pouring samples. General Admission covers 12 whiskey samples and unlimited food. All-Inclusive ($95) is unlimited everything plus commemorative glassware and VIP seating. Live music, 5–8pm. Strictly 21+. Proceeds benefit The Chattanooga Market nonprofit. Tickets through chattanoogafestivals.com/bacon, non-refundable.

title: Chattanooga Beer Fest
description: Chattanooga Beer Fest at First Horizon Pavilion on May 23 — 31 breweries, unlimited samples, collector glass, and live music. Capped at 1,300 people and sold out every year since 2021.
body: 31 breweries, mostly from Tennessee, Georgia, Alabama, and North Carolina, alongside nationals like Dogfish Head, Lagunitas, Sam Adams, and Sierra Nevada. Unlimited samples, collector tasting glass, three food trucks (Wei To Go, The Bistro, Windy City Eats), and live reggae rock from Fresh Mind. Capped at 1,300. It has sold out every year from 2021 through 2025. $48 advance, $55 at the door if any remain, $20 designated driver. Buy only through chattanoogabeerfest.com. 21+ only.

title: Chattanooga Cocktail Festival
description: The Chattanooga Cocktail Festival at First Horizon Pavilion on May 9 — a passport for 12 mini cocktails from local distilleries and top bartenders, plus mixology competitions and live entertainment. 21+ only.
body: Your ticket is a passport for 12 mini cocktails from local distilleries and bartenders. Ketel One, Bulleit, Empress Gin, tequilas, and more in the mix. Mixology competitions, live entertainment, and food trucks on site. Proceeds benefit the Chattanooga Market nonprofit. Strictly 21+, physical ID required. Presented by Chattanooga Festivals, the same crew behind the Bacon & Barrel event.

title: Chattanooga Motorcar Festival
description: The Chattanooga Motorcar Festival takes over the downtown riverfront for a weekend of vintage racing, Concours d'Elegance, and car culture. Debuted 2019, returning Fall 2026.
body: Vintage racing on track, a Concours d'Elegance drawing entries from across the country, automobile displays, and concerts on the downtown riverfront. The festival debuted in 2019 and ran every fall until a postponement in 2025. The 2024 Best in Show went to a 1935 Swallow Sidecar SS1. Returning Fall 2026. Specific dates haven't been announced yet. Check chattanoogamotorcar.com for updates.

title: Ketner's Mill Country Arts Fair
description: Ketner's Mill Country Arts Fair returns October 3-4, 2026 in Whitwell, TN. 48th annual fair at the historic 1824 grist mill — 150+ artisans, sorghum demos, bluegrass, wagon rides, and southern fair food in the Sequatchie Valley.
body: An 1824 water-powered grist mill in the Sequatchie Valley, about 45 minutes from Chattanooga, hosts this every October. Over 150 juried artisans sell paintings, pottery, woodworking, jewelry, and folk art. Sorghum molasses gets made on site with mule-powered equipment. Wagon and canoe rides run on the Sequatchie River, the Marion County 4-H brings a petting zoo, and live bluegrass, country, and gospel plays all weekend. $8 cash at the gate, kids 8 and under free. All admission goes toward preserving the mill. Saturday 9am–6pm, Sunday 10am–5:30pm. Free parking, leashed dogs welcome.

title: MAINx24
description: MAINx24 is a 24-hour street festival on the Chattanooga Southside every first Saturday of December. 120+ events including the parade, Chili Cook-Off, Adult Big Wheel Races, and concerts on Main Street.
body: Main Street on the Southside goes car-free for 24 hours every first Saturday of December. What started as a handful of events has grown to 120+: parade (voted best in Chattanooga), Chili Cook-Off, Adult Big Wheel Races, concerts, arts, and general shenanigans spread across the neighborhood. Free. December 5, 2026.

title: National Cornbread Festival
description: The 29th annual National Cornbread Festival in South Pittsburg, TN — 30 miles west of Chattanooga. National cook-off, Cornbread Alley samples, live music, 5K, and a weekend built around Lodge Cast Iron's hometown.
body: South Pittsburg is the historic home of Lodge Cast Iron, and every last full weekend of April the town leans into it hard. The National Cornbread Cook-Off, Cornbread Alley where civic groups hand out creative variations, live music, a 5K, and vendor shopping fill two days in town. About 30 miles west of Chattanooga. Saturday 8am–6:30pm, Sunday 8am–5pm. Free parking with shuttle from outer lots. Rain or shine, no pets. Presale tickets through TicketSpice.

title: Tennessee Strawberry Festival
description: The 79th annual Tennessee Strawberry Festival runs May 4-9, 2026 in historic downtown Dayton, TN. A week of parade, pageants, carnival, baking contest, live music, and fresh strawberries — a small-town tradition over 75 years running.
body: Dayton, TN has been doing this for 79 years. A full week in downtown built around fresh strawberries: grand parade, pageants, carnival rides in Washington Park, art show, baking contest, cruise-in, and food vendors. The Kentucky Headhunters headline Saturday night. About 45 minutes north of Chattanooga. The week runs Monday May 4 through Saturday May 9. Saturday is the big day, starting with a pancake breakfast at 7:30am and the Strawberry Chase 5K at 8am before the headliner closes it out.

title: Wine Over Water
description: Wine Over Water returns October 10, 2026 at Renaissance Park in Chattanooga. 30th anniversary of the region's premier wine tasting event — curated pours, food by Whitebird's Chef Amanda Clayton, and live music. 21+ only.
body: Thirty years of wine on the Tennessee River. Curated tastings with a commemorative glass, small bites and food pairings by Chef Amanda Clayton of Whitebird, charcuterie, pulled pork, live music from Ben van Winkle and The Figments, and roaming performances by the Chattanooga Circus Collective. The 2026 edition moves from the Walnut Street Bridge to Renaissance Park, between the Walnut Street and Market Street Bridges, while the bridge is under renovation. Same riverfront setting, different footprint. 21+ only, tickets through Eventbrite, nonrefundable but transferable. Presented by Preserve Chattanooga, platinum sponsor Food City.

title: Chattanooga Market — Beast Feast BBQ Festival
description: The Chattanooga Market's Beast Feast BBQ Festival at First Horizon Pavilion on July 19 — a barbecue competition with local pitmasters, vendors, and food.
body: The Chattanooga Market's Beast Feast BBQ Festival lands at First Horizon Pavilion on July 19, a barbecue competition with local pitmasters going head to head alongside the regular vendor market. Free, 11am–4pm.

title: Chattanooga Market — Father's Day Blues & Brews
description: The Chattanooga Market's Father's Day Blues & Brews at First Horizon Pavilion on June 21. Live blues music, craft brews, local vendors, and fresh produce.
body: Blues music and craft brews at the Chattanooga Market, June 21 at First Horizon Pavilion. Local vendors and fresh produce fill the rest. Free, 11am–4pm.

title: Chattanooga Market — FiveStar Food Fight
description: The Chattanooga Market's FiveStar Food Fight at First Horizon Pavilion on June 28 — a culinary competition alongside local vendors, fresh produce, and food.
body: The Chattanooga Market's FiveStar Food Fight lands at First Horizon Pavilion on June 28. A culinary competition at the center, vendors and fresh produce filling the rest of the market. Free, 11am–4pm.

title: Chattanooga Market — Midsummer Solstice
description: The Chattanooga Market's Midsummer Solstice edition at First Horizon Pavilion on June 14. Local vendors, fresh produce, food, and live music celebrating the height of summer.
body: The Chattanooga Market marks midsummer at First Horizon Pavilion on June 14, with local vendors, fresh produce, food, and live music dressed up for the occasion. Free, 11am–4pm.

title: Chattanooga Market — Peach Festival
description: The Chattanooga Market's Peach Festival at First Horizon Pavilion on July 12 — peak-season peaches, local vendors, food, and live music.
body: The Chattanooga Market's annual Peach Festival hits First Horizon Pavilion on July 12 at peak peach season. Fresh peaches take center stage, local vendors and food fill out the rest. Free, 11am–4pm.

title: Chattanooga Market — Red, White and Blueberries
description: The Chattanooga Market's Red, White and Blueberries edition at First Horizon Pavilion on July 5. A patriotic-themed summer market with local vendors, fresh blueberries, and food.
body: The Chattanooga Market's post-Fourth celebration runs at First Horizon Pavilion on July 5. Patriotic theme, fresh blueberries front and center, local vendors, and food. Free, 11am–4pm.

title: Chattanooga Market — Singer Songwriter Sunday
description: The Chattanooga Market's Singer Songwriter Sunday at First Horizon Pavilion on July 26 — live original music from local and regional songwriters alongside vendors and food.
body: The Chattanooga Market spotlights local and regional songwriters at First Horizon Pavilion on July 26. Live original music up front, vendors and food throughout. Free, 11am–4pm.

title: Sunday Patio Music
description: Free live music on the patio every Sunday from 1 to 4pm at Five Wits Brewing Company, featuring local Chattanooga musicians.
body: Sundays slow down on the Five Wits patio on Long Street. Local musicians play from 1 to 4pm while the taps stay busy. Claim a table outside, bring a friend, and let the afternoon stretch on. No cover, so wander in and stay a while.

title: Trivia Night at Five Wits
description: Free trivia night every Thursday at 7pm at Five Wits Brewing Company, hosted by Chatt Trivia with prizes for the top three teams.
body: Thursday nights mean trivia at Five Wits on Long Street. Chatt Trivia hosts from 7 to 9pm. Answer well and your team lands in the top three for prizes. Grab a pint and claim a table early. Free to play, so round up a sharp crew.

title: Fall Festival at Flat Top Mountain Farm
description: Fall festival weekends at Flat Top Mountain Farm in Soddy-Daisy, TN — pumpkin patch, hayrides, corn maze, and mountain views.
body: Flat Top runs fall weekends through September and October — pumpkin patch, hayrides with views out to the Smoky Mountains, a corn maze, flower fields, food trucks, and local vendors. $12 admission. About 20 minutes north of Chattanooga in Soddy-Daisy.

title: Harvest Hustle 5K
description: Off-road 5K through Flat Top Mountain Farm in Soddy-Daisy, TN on September 27.
body: Off-road 5K through the farm fields at Flat Top Mountain, with the sunflower fields and mountain views as the backdrop. The course runs past grazing horses and alongside the Blue Ridge Mountains in the distance. Register through RunSignUp.

title: Autumn in Watercolor: Plein Air Workshop
description: Plein air watercolor workshop at Happy Valley Farms in Rossville, GA with nationally acclaimed watercolorist Alan Shuptrine.
body: Paint the countryside with nationally acclaimed watercolorist Alan Shuptrine. The workshop runs five hours with live demonstrations and personal instruction on the Happy Valley property. $175 covers all instruction — bring your own supplies or ask about what to bring when you register.

title: Barbecue & Bourbon Dinner
description: Farm-to-table four-course dinner at Happy Valley Farms in Rossville, GA with pitmaster Chris Prieto, bourbon cocktails, and live music.
body: Four courses with award-winning pitmaster Chris Prieto — smoked brisket, farm-sourced sides, specialty bourbon cocktails, and live music against the sunflower fields. Happy Valley is just over the Georgia line, about 15 minutes from downtown Chattanooga. $225 per person, ticketed.

title: Art + Issues: Creating Caring Communities
description: Art + Issues is a discussion on creating caring communities at the Hunter Museum on August 20.
body: Art + Issues comes back August 20 with a talk on building communities that actually look after each other. The series pins art to the real questions facing Chattanooga. Sit and listen or jump into the discussion. Either way you leave with more than you walked in with.

title: Art Wise: U.S. 250th
description: Art Wise: U.S. 250th is a guided art talk at the Hunter Museum on September 10 marking the nation's 250th year.
body: Art Wise: U.S. 250th takes a closer look at American art on September 10 as the country nears its 250th year. A guide walks you through the work and shares the stories behind it. Come ready to look, listen, and ask questions.

title: Co-Creating an Empathic Community
description: A collaborative community event at the Hunter Museum on August 27.
body: This one puts your hands on the wheel instead of just watching. On August 27 the Hunter invites you to help shape a more empathic community, working shoulder to shoulder with the other people who showed up. Check the museum site for the format and start time before you head over.

title: Crafts & Coffee
description: Crafts & Coffee is a relaxed morning of art making at the Hunter Museum on September 4.
body: Crafts & Coffee gives you a slow morning at the Hunter Museum on September 4. Grab a hot cup, sit down at a table, and make something small with your hands. It is easy, it is social, and you do not need any art skills to join in.

title: Make and Move Monday
description: Make and Move Monday pairs art projects with movement for families at the Hunter Museum on September 7.
body: Make and Move Monday mixes hands-on art with a little bit of moving around on September 7. Kids build something at the table, then get up and shake out the wiggles. It is a good fit for young families looking to start the week at the museum.

title: Plants for Healing and the Art of Saya Woolfalk at Crabtree Farms
description: An off-site event on healing plants and the art of Saya Woolfalk at Crabtree Farms on September 5.
body: This one leaves the bluff and heads to Crabtree Farms on September 5. The day links healing plants in the ground to the art of Saya Woolfalk. Spend it outdoors with your hands in the dirt, connecting the garden back to the gallery. Check the museum site for timing and how to sign up.

title: Throwback Thursday and Saya Woolfalk: A Musical Experience
description: A musical experience tied to the Saya Woolfalk exhibition at the Hunter Museum on September 3.
body: The Hunter turns Throwback Thursday into a music night on September 3. Live sound fills the galleries and ties into the Saya Woolfalk exhibition. Wander with the art and the music sharing the same room. The museum site has the start time and any ticket details.

title: Wreaths and Art at Walden Peak Farm
description: Wreaths and Art at Walden Peak Farm is an off-site art and craft outing hosted by the Hunter Museum on September 19.
body: Wreaths and Art at Walden Peak Farm takes the museum outdoors on September 19. Spend the day making a wreath and looking at art on the farm. It is a hands-on trip that pairs the Hunter Museum with a working farm setting.

title: Hutton & Smith Bike Night
description: Bike Night every Tuesday starting at 6pm at Hutton & Smith Brewing Co. on the Southside. Ride in, grab a $3 pint, and hang with the local cycling crowd. Dogs welcome, 21+.
body: Bike Night at Hutton and Smith every Tuesday starting at 6pm. Cyclists roll in, $3 pints are on, and the patio fills up with riders from across the Southside. Dogs welcome. Free to attend. 21+.

title: Hutton & Smith Thursday Trivia
description: Free trivia every Thursday at 7pm at Hutton & Smith Brewing Co. on the Southside. Dogs welcome, 21+.
body: Free trivia every Thursday night at 7pm at Hutton and Smith Brewing on the Southside. Bring a crew, grab a pint, and see what you know. Questions run across categories, not just sports. Dogs welcome. 21+.

title: Giveback Night with La Paz
description: Giveback Night at Oddstory Brewing with La Paz on August 20 at 5pm. A pint supports a good cause in Chattanooga.
body: Oddstory teams up with La Paz for a Giveback Night on August 20 starting at 5pm. Grab a beer and a bite knowing a share heads back to the community work La Paz does around town. Easy way to do a little good on Campbell St.

title: Kid Clothing Swap
description: Kid Clothing Swap at Oddstory Brewing on August 22 at 2pm. Bring outgrown kids clothes, take what you need. Free.
body: Bring the clothes your kids blew through and swap for the next size up at Oddstory on August 22 at 2pm. No money changes hands — just haul in what no longer fits and dig for what does. Free, and the taps are open for the grownups.

title: Oddstory Monday BINGO
description: Free BINGO every Monday at 6:30pm at Oddstory Brewing Co. A great way to kick off the week.
body: BINGO every Monday at 6:30pm at Oddstory Brewing on Campbell St. Cold beer, free to play, and a crowd that takes the numbers surprisingly seriously. Good way to ease into the week without too much lollygagging.

title: Oddstory Pub Trivia
description: Free pub trivia every Tuesday and Thursday at 7:30pm at Oddstory Brewing Co.
body: Pub trivia twice a week at Oddstory on Campbell St, every Tuesday and Thursday at 7:30pm. Grab a pint and bring a crew with a hodgepodge of knowledge. The questions span categories. Free to play.

title: Jammin' At The Barnyard
description: Live music, farm-fresh food, and a summer evening at Quail Run Farm in Chattanooga.
body: Live music on the farm with a food truck serving Quail Run's own beef and pork. BYOB, bring a blanket or chairs. A real farm property about 15 minutes from downtown — check their site for availability as it tends to sell out.

title: Autumn Equinox Event for Members
description: A members-only evening at Reflection Riding to mark the autumn equinox with native plants, tea, and yoga.
body: Members gather to mark the turn of the season. The evening brings native plant activities, herbal teas, and a guided yoga session. The light fades slow over the grounds as fall sets in. This one is open to Reflection Riding members only.

title: Campfire Concert: Barefoot Nellie
description: An outdoor evening concert at Reflection Riding featuring Barefoot Nellie.
body: Spread a blanket and settle in for live music under the open sky. Barefoot Nellie plays as the sun drops behind the ridge. Food and drink are part of the evening on the grounds. Bring the family and stay until the last song.

title: Campfire Concert: Donna the Buffalo
description: An outdoor evening concert at Reflection Riding featuring Donna the Buffalo.
body: Donna the Buffalo brings their roots sound to the grounds. Spread a blanket and enjoy live music as the evening cools. Food and drink are part of the night at Reflection Riding. Stay for the whole set as the stars come out.

title: Campfire Concert: Jon Stickley Trio
description: An outdoor evening concert at Reflection Riding featuring the Jon Stickley Trio.
body: The Jon Stickley Trio plays fast, sharp acoustic music under the open sky. Bring a chair and settle in for the evening. Food and drink round out the night at Reflection Riding. The picking gets wild once the sun goes down.

title: Campfire Concert: Kasvot Chätt
description: An outdoor evening concert at Reflection Riding featuring Kasvot Chätt.
body: Close out the concert season with Kasvot Chätt. Bring a blanket and enjoy live music in the cool night air. Food and drink are part of the evening at Reflection Riding. Send the fall series off with one last night under the stars.

title: Campfire Concert: Yarn
description: An outdoor evening concert at Reflection Riding featuring the band Yarn.
body: Bring a chair and enjoy live music in the open air. Yarn plays deep into the evening on the grounds at Reflection Riding. Food and drink round out the night. Come early, grab a spot, and watch the sky change color.

title: Crabtree Farms Fall Plant Sale
description: A weekend fall plant sale at Reflection Riding with native plants from Crabtree Farms.
body: Stock up on native plants for the fall planting season. Crabtree Farms brings a big selection across the whole weekend. Staff help you pick plants that fit your yard and soil. Fall is the best time to get roots in the ground.

title: Give Back Night at Oddstory Central
description: A fundraising night for Reflection Riding at Oddstory Brewing's Central taproom.
body: Grab a beer and put it toward a good cause. Oddstory's Central taproom hosts the night and gives back a share of sales. Come out, raise a glass, and support Reflection Riding. Bring friends and make an easy night count.

title: Green|Spaces Lunch and Learn
description: A midday session at Reflection Riding about its mission and sustainability work, with Green|Spaces.
body: Bring your lunch and learn how Reflection Riding cares for its land. Staff share the site's mission and the daily work behind it. Green|Spaces joins to talk about sustainability in and around Chattanooga. The session runs one hour, so you can eat and get back to your day.

title: Hard of Hearing Night: Owl Odyssey
description: An evening Owl Odyssey program at Reflection Riding with ASL interpretation, open to all.
body: This evening owl program includes ASL interpretation and welcomes everyone. Learn how barn owls hunt in the dark and raise their young. A guide brings an owl out for a close look. The hour moves at a relaxed pace after the sun goes down.

title: Hard of Hearing Night: Winged Wisdom
description: An evening birds-of-prey program at Reflection Riding with ASL interpretation, open to all.
body: This evening program covers local birds of prey and includes ASL interpretation. Everyone is welcome to attend. You learn how raptors hunt and survive the winter. A guide brings a bird out for a close look before the hour ends.

title: Healing with Nature with The Chattery
description: A guided outdoor wellness session at Reflection Riding, presented with The Chattery.
body: Step outside and let the pace drop. This session with The Chattery uses the trails and gardens to settle the mind and body. A guide leads simple activities over two easy hours. You leave with small ways to bring nature into daily life.

title: Introduction to Hula with The Chattery
description: A one-hour intro to Hawaiian hula dance at Reflection Riding, presented with The Chattery.
body: Learn the basics of hula in one easy hour. This friendly class with The Chattery covers simple steps and the stories behind the dance. No experience is needed, so anyone can join in. You leave with moves you can practice at home.

title: Master Gardener Series: Amazing Grasses
description: A Master Gardener talk at Reflection Riding on low-maintenance native grasses.
body: Native grasses add texture and ask for almost no care. This talk covers which grasses grow well here and how to use them. A Master Gardener leads the one hour session. You leave with a short list ready for your own yard.

title: Master Gardener Series: Give Yourself a Fighting Chance Against Invasive Plants
description: A Master Gardener talk at Reflection Riding on how to manage invasive plants in your own yard.
body: Invasive plants take over a yard fast. A Master Gardener shows you how to spot them early and stop them for good. You get clear steps you can use at home this season. Bring your questions about the plants giving you trouble.

title: Music in the Wild
description: An outdoor performance at Reflection Riding inspired by "Peter and the Wolf," with the Chattanooga Symphony & Opera.
body: The Chattanooga Symphony & Opera brings music straight into the woods. The program draws on "Peter and the Wolf" and fits the wild setting. Bring the family and a blanket for the afternoon. Kids can hear the story told through the orchestra.

title: Nursery Workshop: Propagation Intensive
description: A hands-on plant propagation workshop with the nursery team at Reflection Riding.
body: Learn how to grow new plants from cuttings and seed. The nursery team shows you the same methods they use every day. You get hands on practice over the afternoon. Take your new skills home and fill your own garden for free.

title: Oli Kai Trail Race
description: A timed trail running event at Reflection Riding with 3, 6, and 9-hour options on a 2.1-mile loop.
body: Run as far as your legs will carry you on a 2.1 mile forest loop. Pick the 3, 6, or 9 hour option and set your own pace. The trail winds through the woods at Reflection Riding. Every lap adds to your total distance.

title: Oli Via Half Marathon and 4.5-Mile Trail Race
description: A trail race day at Reflection Riding offering a half marathon and a 4.5-mile course.
body: Choose the half marathon or the shorter 4.5 mile course. Both routes run through the trails and open ground at Reflection Riding. Roots, creeks, and quiet woods keep every mile interesting. Runners of all levels are welcome to line up.

title: Owl Odyssey
description: An afternoon program at Reflection Riding about barn owls and how they live in the wild.
body: Get to know the barn owl over one quiet hour. This program covers how these silent hunters find food and raise their young. A guide brings an owl out so you can see it up close. You leave knowing why owls matter to the land around Chattanooga.

title: Project ReWild
description: A hands-on habitat restoration morning at Reflection Riding focused on removing invasive plants.
body: Roll up your sleeves and give native habitat a fighting chance. Volunteers pull invasive plants and put native species back in the soil. Staff show you how invasive plants spread and how to stop them. You can use the same tricks in your own yard.

title: Spirits and Sustainability with Green|Spaces
description: An evening at Reflection Riding on its mission and sustainability work, with light refreshments.
body: Learn how Reflection Riding protects native land and wildlife. Green|Spaces leads the talk over light refreshments. You hear real steps the site takes to stay green. The evening runs two hours on the grounds, so come unwind and listen.

title: Tails, Trails, and Ales
description: A dog-friendly trail race day at Reflection Riding, presented by Mountain View Ford.
body: Bring your dog and hit the trails together. This race day lets you run with your four legged friend across the grounds. Mountain View Ford presents the event at Reflection Riding. Cross the finish line, then grab an ale to celebrate.

title: Wild Ones Plant Sale
description: A native plant sale at Reflection Riding featuring selections from the Wild Ones group.
body: Find native plants that feed local birds and pollinators. The Wild Ones group brings a strong selection to this one day sale. Volunteers help you choose plants that fit your space. Every plant you take home gives wildlife a place to land.

title: Wild Wonders: A Close Encounter with Native Animals
description: A guided tour of the Native Animal Area at Reflection Riding to meet resident animal ambassadors.
body: Walk the Native Animal Area and meet the resident ambassadors up close. A guide shares each animal's story and its place in the local food web. You see turtles, snakes, and other creatures that call this land home. Time slots run at 11am and again at 1pm.

title: Winged Wisdom: Understanding Birds of Prey
description: A morning program at Reflection Riding about local birds of prey and their role in the ecosystem.
body: Meet the hawks, owls, and falcons that hunt around Chattanooga. A guide brings live raptors out and explains how each one finds food. You learn why these birds keep the local food web in balance. The program runs one hour on the grounds at Reflection Riding.

title: Appalachian Floor Brooms
description: Half-day broom-making workshop at Sequatchie Cove Farm — bind local broomcorn into a hand-carved heirloom broom.
body: Learn to make an Appalachian floor broom with Ali Davenport — local broomcorn, hand-carved handles, bound the traditional way. Timed for the fall equinox. Half-day, you leave with a broom that'll outlast anything from a hardware store.

title: Baking with Freshly Milled Grains
description: Afternoon baking workshop at Sequatchie Cove Farm on milling and baking with fresh wheat from Neidlovs Bakery.
body: Erik Zilen of Neidlovs Bakery walks through milling and baking with freshly milled wheat. Three and a half hours on a Saturday afternoon — good intro if you've been curious about grain-to-loaf baking but haven't known where to start.

title: Build a Cumberland Foot Stool
description: Full-day chair-making workshop at Sequatchie Cove Farm — build a 3-leg wooden footstool using mostly hand tools.
body: Spend the day with Tyler Rogers learning basic chair-making technique. You'll build a 3-legged Cumberland footstool using mostly hand tools and leave with it. No experience needed. Sequatchie Cove runs these workshops year-round — this is one of the better ones for learning a durable skill.

title: Dances from Around the World
description: Community dance workshop at Sequatchie Cove Farm with Anna Claire Camp, covering folk dances from Russia, Germany, Scotland, Denmark, and Appalachia.
body: Anna Claire Camp teaches community dances from Russia, Germany, Scotland, Denmark, and Appalachia. No partner and no experience needed — these are group dances made for beginners. A good excuse to move and meet people out at the farm.

title: Fermenting the Harvest with Sandor Katz
description: Full-day fermentation workshop at Sequatchie Cove Farm with fermentation revivalist Sandor Katz.
body: Sandor Katz literally wrote the book on fermentation. This is a full-day hands-on session at Sequatchie Cove — kraut, kimchi, and other techniques demystified by the person who brought fermentation back into mainstream food culture. Worth the drive.

title: Making a Galette
description: Half-day workshop at Sequatchie Cove Farm on rough puff pastry and rustic galettes with Mallory Grimm Tubbs.
body: Learn rough puff pastry and how to shape and fill a galette with Mallory Grimm Tubbs. Four hours, hands-on, you leave with something to eat. Good timing for fall produce.

title: Knitting for Beginners: Washcloths
description: Beginner knitting workshop at Sequatchie Cove Farm with Tracy Knutson — learn basic stitches by making a small washcloth.
body: Tracy Knutson teaches the basics of knitting through one small, useful project — a washcloth or dishcloth. You learn to cast on, knit, and bind off, and you leave with something you can actually use. No experience needed.

title: Linoleum Block Prints
description: Block printing workshop at Sequatchie Cove Farm with Laurel York — carve a linoleum block and pull your own prints.
body: Laurel York walks you through carving a design into linoleum and pulling your own block prints. You learn how to transfer a design, carve it safely, and ink and press it onto paper. You leave with prints you made by hand.

title: Reading the Woods: Plant Identification
description: Morning walk through Sequatchie Valley with botanist Cooper Breeden covering tree, shrub, and vine identification.
body: A four-hour morning walk through the Sequatchie Valley with Cooper Breeden, focused on identifying the trees, shrubs, and vines that grow here. Good for anyone who spends time in Tennessee woods and wants to know what they're looking at.

title: Stained Glass Stars
description: Full-day Tiffany method stained glass workshop at Sequatchie Cove Farm — make a 3D glass star.
body: Learn Tiffany method stained glass with Tammy O'Connor and build a three-dimensional glass star over the course of the day. No experience required — the farm's workshop space handles the setup, you handle the cutting and soldering.

title: Soldiers & Sailors Memorial Auditorium: Chicago
description: The legendary rock band Chicago performs live.
body: A 1924 memorial auditorium on McCallie Avenue that seats around 2,000. Named for veterans of World War I, it books a wide range of touring acts — Broadway runs, classic rock, country, and comedy. Bigger and more traditional than the Walker Theatre a few blocks away on Broad Street.

title: Soldiers & Sailors Memorial Auditorium: Mrs. Doubtfire (Touring)
description: Broadway touring production of Mrs. Doubtfire. Opening night.
body: A 1924 memorial auditorium on McCallie Avenue that seats around 2,000. Named for veterans of World War I, it books a wide range of touring acts — Broadway runs, classic rock, country, and comedy. Bigger and more traditional than the Walker Theatre a few blocks away on Broad Street.

title: Augustana (20th Anniversary Tour)
description: Augustana plays Songbirds on August 19 on their 20th Anniversary Tour.
body: Augustana made 'Boston' twenty years ago and it still holds up. They're touring it and playing Songbirds — a room that's the right size for a band reconnecting with the catalog. If you know the record, this is worth it.

title: Chattanooga Horn Authority
description: Chattanooga Horn Authority plays Songbirds on September 5 at 7pm downtown.
body: The Chattanooga Horn Authority packs a big-band brass punch into Songbirds on September 5 at 7pm. Local players, tight charts, and a whole lot of horn on the W Main stage. See the venue site for details.

title: Chelsea Drugstore: The Music of the Rolling Stones
description: Chattanooga's own Chelsea Drugstore plays a full Rolling Stones tribute show at Songbirds on June 26.
body: The riffs, the swagger, the full Stones catalog. Chelsea Drugstore plays it straight without shortcuts. A Chattanooga act that's been doing this long enough to know which songs actually land.

title: Copeland w/ Jenny Dee
description: Copeland plays Songbirds on September 11 with special guest Jenny Dee.
body: Copeland brings their Florida rock to Songbirds on September 11 at 7pm, with special guest Jenny Dee. The band has played together since 2001 and has six albums to draw from. It is a full sound in a close room. Tickets on the venue site.

title: Dock Party w/ Belle Vista
description: Dock Party, a six-piece Oasis tribute, plays Songbirds on July 10 with Belle Vista supporting.
body: Dock Party plays Oasis covers with six pieces and the swagger to back it up. They know the catalog and they play it loud. Belle Vista opens. 8pm start, so no rushing dinner.

title: Eric Johanson
description: Blues guitarist Eric Johanson plays Songbirds on August 18.
body: Eric Johanson is a New Orleans blues guitarist who plays slide like it's a conversation. His records are good — live is where it actually opens up. Two hours at Songbirds is the right amount of time.

title: Hotel Burgundy
description: Hotel Burgundy plays Songbirds on August 20.
body: Hotel Burgundy at Songbirds on a Thursday. They've been building a following on the road and this is a good room to see them in before the venues get bigger. Get there early.

title: Hudson Macready w/ Charlie George
description: Hudson Macready plays Songbirds on August 21 with Charlie George opening.
body: Hudson Macready plays a Friday night at Songbirds with Charlie George opening. Two songwriters, one room. The kind of bill where the opener stays and the headliner shows up early.

title: John Cowan Trio
description: John Cowan Trio plays Songbirds on September 4 at 7pm in downtown Chattanooga.
body: John Cowan — the New Grass Revival voice — brings his trio to Songbirds on September 4 at 7pm. Decades of high-lonesome harmony and bluegrass fire in a room small enough to feel every note. Tickets on the venue site.

title: Laid Back Country Picker
description: Laid Back Country Picker plays country and rockabilly at Songbirds on June 17. As heard on Sirius Outlaw Country.
body: Country and rockabilly with enough edge for Sirius Outlaw Country. Laid Back Country Picker has a loose road feel to them, and Drummer Honey is the anchor of the outfit. Tuesday night at Songbirds on June 17.

title: Monday Night Social
description: Monday Night Social performs their album Chasing Light in its entirety at Songbirds on June 5.
body: Monday Night Social takes the Songbirds stage on a June weeknight to perform their second album Chasing Light front to back. If you haven't heard the record, this is a good way to get the full thing in one sitting.

title: Nolan Taylor w/ Jess Woodland
description: Nolan Taylor plays Songbirds on September 10 with Jess Woodland opening.
body: Nolan Taylor plays Songbirds on September 10 at 7pm, with Jess Woodland opening. His songs put a voice to people who often go unheard. The room stays small, so every word lands. Tickets on the venue site.

title: Paul McDonald & the Mourning Doves
description: Paul McDonald & the Mourning Doves play Songbirds on June 27 with Southern-rooted rock and soul.
body: Paul McDonald came up through American Idol, but the live show is a different thing. The Mourning Doves back him with Southern rock and soul, and together they've got a sound that holds up on the road. Songbirds on June 27.

title: PLVNET w/ Hour Late
description: PLVNET plays Songbirds on August 22 with Hour Late opening.
body: PLVNET brings their sound to Songbirds with Hour Late opening the night. Saturday show, two acts, and a venue that keeps it close. Worth checking their catalog before you go.

title: The Long Run
description: The Long Run, an Eagles tribute band, live at Songbirds. Note: this show has been postponed — check the venue for updated dates.
body: The Long Run is an Eagles tribute band known for spot-on harmonies and masterful guitar work recreating the Eagles' iconic sound. This show was listed as postponed — check Songbirds' website for a rescheduled date.

title: The New Quintet w/ Brother and the Hayes
description: The New Quintet plays Songbirds on August 28 with Brother and the Hayes opening.
body: The New Quintet at Songbirds with Brother and the Hayes opening. Jazz and soul on a Friday — the kind of night that doesn't need a big crowd to feel full. Songbirds is a good room for it.

title: Tyler Ramsey & Carl Broemel — Celestun Tour
description: Tyler Ramsey and Carl Broemel of My Morning Jacket bring the Celestun Tour to Songbirds on June 23.
body: Tyler Ramsey and Carl Broemel of My Morning Jacket are touring together behind the Celestun project. Two guitar players, one stage, no backing tracks. They both have strong solo followings, and this is a chance to hear what happens when they share the set. Songbirds on June 23.

title: Vincen Garcia
description: Spanish bassist Vincen Garcia brings his modern jazz and funk sound to Songbirds on June 16.
body: A Spanish bassist who moves between jazz and funk, with a resume built at major festivals across Europe and beyond. Vincen Garcia at Songbirds is a small room for a player at this level. June 16.

title: WOMB
description: WOMB plays Songbirds on August 14.
body: WOMB at Songbirds on a Friday night. The room's capacity keeps it close, and this is the kind of act that rewards being in the front. Worth checking out early.

title: ZG Smith and Madison Hughes
description: Americana duo ZG Smith and Madison Hughes at Songbirds on June 11. Hughes is a veteran of The Voice.
body: ZG Smith and Madison Hughes play Americana with a lot of road time behind it. Madison Hughes came up through The Voice. Two performers who've been doing this long enough to know how to use a small room. Songbirds on June 11.

title: The Walker Theatre: Bobby Stone Film Series: The Godfather Part II
description: Coppola's 1974 sequel — still the rare follow-up that matches the original. Al Pacino and Robert De Niro.
body: A 1921 theater on Broad Street that spent a century as the Tivoli before reopening as The Walker Theatre in 2024. The restored interior seats around 1,700 and hosts a mix of concerts, comedy, and the Bobby Stone Film Series — a curated run of cinema that leans toward the artful, queer, and cult. The Bobby Stone Film Series is the main recurring thing here. Named for a local benefactor, it brings in films you won't catch at a multiplex — double features on Friday nights, solo screenings on Sunday afternoons. Tickets are cheap compared to concerts.

description: 3 Star Revival brings Tennessee funk and groove to WanderLinger Brewing on August 22 at 9pm. $10 cover in Chattanooga's Southside.
body: 3 Star Revival takes the WanderLinger stage on August 22 at 9pm with their brand of Tennessee funk and groove. The band leans hard on improvisation, so no two sets sound the same. Settle in with a beer and let the groove ride. $10 gets you in the door on Station Street.

title: Dead Cover Office
description: Dead Cover Office plays Grateful Dead classics at WanderLinger Brewing on November 7 at 6pm. No cover, all ages, in Chattanooga's Southside.
body: Dead Cover Office brings the Grateful Dead songbook to WanderLinger on November 7 from 6 to 9pm. Expect fan favorites and plenty of improvisational jamming. There is no cover and the show is all ages, so bring the whole crew to Station Street.

title: Dubstep Night
description: LFO Collective brings a heavy bass dubstep night to WanderLinger Brewing on August 22 at 9pm. $10 cover, 21+, in Chattanooga's Southside.
body: LFO Collective takes over WanderLinger on August 22 at 9pm for a night of heavy bass. The lineup stacks UP TEN, DVBBY DOO, SPACEPAK, JAWNRA, and SKALD back to back. This one is 21 and up, and $10 gets you in the door on Station Street.

title: The Loop
description: The Loop brings nearly 70 vintage motorcycles from 1930 to 1959 to WanderLinger Brewing on September 6. Vendors, an artisan market, and live music.
body: The Loop rolls into WanderLinger on September 6 from 2 to 8pm with nearly 70 vintage motorcycles built between 1930 and 1959. Vintage vendors and an artisan market fill out the day. Gino Fanelli plays live at 5pm, so grab a beer on Station Street and take it all in.

description: Every Friday at 8pm at The Woodshop Listening Room in St. Elmo. Rotating regional musicians playing traditional bluegrass. $5 cover.
body: Regional musicians rotating through The Woodshop every Friday night in St. Elmo. Traditional bluegrass in a small listening room, doors at 8pm. $5 cover at the door. The room is intimate enough that there's no bad seat in the house.

title: Scenic City Soul Night
description: Scenic City Soul Night every Thursday at 8pm at The Woodshop Listening Room. Bryant 'Bass Hitter' Russell brings '70s Motown, jazz, and smooth soul. $10 cover.
body: Bryant 'Bass Hitter' Russell and his band bring the groove every Thursday at The Woodshop in St. Elmo. The setlist runs through '70s Motown, jazz, and smooth soul. Intimate listening room, $10 cover, doors at 8pm.

body: Jhett Black plays blues every Tuesday night at The Woodshop in St. Elmo. Small room, close sound, doors at 8pm. $10 cover at the door, or reserve a table if you want a guaranteed seat. Runs late enough to feel like a proper Tuesday.

title: Daniel Kimbro & Sam Lewis
description: Daniel Kimbro and Sam Lewis at The Woodshop on November 12, a collaborative evening of songwriting about place, time, and the human experience.
body: Daniel Kimbro and Sam Lewis share a stage in St. Elmo for a night of collaborative songwriting. The set digs into place, time, and the human experience. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm.

title: David Grier
description: Flatpick guitar great David Grier at The Woodshop on September 5, a three-time IBMA Guitar Player of the Year.
body: David Grier is widely regarded as one of the finest flatpick guitarists around — a three-time IBMA Guitar Player of the Year. A small room and a lot of guitar. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm.

title: DVL Blues Legends
description: DVL Blues Legends with The DVL Revue at The Woodshop on September 19. A high-energy tribute to Muddy Waters, John Lee Hooker, Howlin' Wolf, and B.B. King.
body: The DVL Revue returns with a high-energy blues tribute in St. Elmo. The set honors Muddy Waters, John Lee Hooker, Howlin' Wolf, and B.B. King. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm.

title: Goldpine
description: Nashville Americana duo Goldpine at The Woodshop on September 13, known for bold harmonies and 'aggressive Americana'.
body: Goldpine is a Nashville husband-and-wife duo trading bold harmonies in what they call 'aggressive Americana.' Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm.

title: Jake Blount
description: Performer and scholar Jake Blount at The Woodshop on September 9, a player of Black folk music who's appeared at Carnegie Hall and Newport Folk Festival.
body: Jake Blount is both a performer and a scholar of Black folk music, with stops at Carnegie Hall and the Newport Folk Festival behind him. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm.

title: Joe Kaplow
description: California singer-songwriter Joe Kaplow at The Woodshop on September 9. Personal narrative rooted in farm life and ocean living.
body: Joe Kaplow writes from specific places — California farm life, the coast — and the specificity is what makes it work. Singer-songwriter set in an intimate listening room. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm.

title: Jonathan Peyton
description: Georgia singer-songwriter Jonathan Peyton at The Woodshop on October 3, with Hunter Blalock opening.
body: Jonathan Peyton is an independent Georgia singer-songwriter who leans on emotionally resonant storytelling. Hunter Blalock opens. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm.

title: Mama's Broke
description: Canadian Folk Music Award winners Mama's Broke at The Woodshop on November 13, with haunting harmonies and deep folk traditions.
body: Mama's Broke are Canadian Folk Music Award winners known for haunting vocal harmonies rooted in older folk traditions. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm.

title: Mid America
description: Western folk rock duo Mid America at The Woodshop on September 18: Mia Carruthers and Curtis Roush with '70s-influenced songwriting.
body: Mid America pairs Mia Carruthers and Curtis Roush for a western folk rock set steeped in '70s-influenced songwriting and timeless harmonies. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm.

title: OBELISK
description: Local drum and bass duo OBELISK at The Woodshop on September 12, playing SciCo fusion and hard jazz. Standing room show.
body: OBELISK is a local drum and bass duo that plays SciCo fusion and hard jazz. This one runs as a standing room show in St. Elmo. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm.

title: Rick Rushing III & The Blues Strangers
description: Chattanooga blues trio Rick Rushing III & The Blues Strangers at The Woodshop on August 22, mixing blues, jazz, rock, and R&B.
body: Rick Rushing III & The Blues Strangers are a Chattanooga trio pulling from blues, jazz, rock, and R&B, with originals and reworked covers in the set. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm.

title: Sherry Cothran
description: Award-winning Americana artist Sherry Cothran at The Woodshop on September 17, blending rock and soul influences.
body: Sherry Cothran is an award-winning Americana artist who folds rock and soul into her songs. She plays the small listening room in St. Elmo. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm.

title: The Encore Sessions
description: The Encore Sessions at The Woodshop on September 2. A free benefit showcase for the Musicians Mental Health Initiative with local artists.
body: Local artists share the stage for a free benefit night in St. Elmo. The show supports the Musicians Mental Health Initiative. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm.

title: The Family
description: The Family at The Woodshop on October 9: four Muscle Shoals musicians — Dylan LeBlanc, James LeBlanc, Angela Hacker, and Bay Simpson — blending '70s folk-rock and soul, recorded at FAME Studios.
body: The Family brings together four Muscle Shoals musicians — Dylan LeBlanc, James LeBlanc, Angela Hacker, and Bay Simpson — for '70s folk-rock with soul in it, recorded at FAME Studios. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm.

title: The Landon Fitzpatrick Band
description: Georgia bluegrass act The Landon Fitzpatrick Band at The Woodshop on August 29, led by an acclaimed banjo player.
body: The Landon Fitzpatrick Band is a Georgia bluegrass act led by an acclaimed banjo player, blending traditional picking with modern originals. Doors at 5pm, show at 6pm.

title: Bats, Beer, & Bluegrass
description: An evening of bluegrass music, cold beer, and bat watching at Fricks Cave Preserve in Chickamauga, GA.
body: Fricks Cave Preserve hosts one of Walker County's most unusual evenings — live bluegrass, cold beer, and watching bats emerge at dusk from one of the region's most significant bat habitats. Tickets available through the Walker Rocks events page.

title: Blue Gray BBQ
description: Blue Gray BBQ at the Gordon Lee Mansion grounds in Chickamauga, GA.
body: The Blue Gray BBQ brings a full day of barbecue to the grounds of the Gordon Lee Mansion in Chickamauga. Check the Walker Rocks events page for entry and tasting details.

title: Chickamauga Birthday Celebration
description: Chickamauga's birthday celebration at the historic Gordon Lee Mansion.
body: Chickamauga celebrates its birthday at the Gordon Lee Mansion. A community afternoon on the historic mansion grounds. Check the Walker Rocks events page for details.

title: Kensington Rodeo
